messages:
sara: Heads-up — noticed a divergence between billing per-token and our runtime token-cost estimates after the kernel-selector rollout. Opening a thread to sync on instrumentation we need to reconcile unit economics.

liam: Can you paste a short reproduction or traces? Is this only on specific routes or global?

sara: Quick summary: token_latency_ms increased for kernel v2 on short sequences (<128). KV cache hit-rate on /translate dropped ~8% for the same window. Billing shows ~+12% per-token cost vs baseline for that customer cohort. I have some stress runs and traces.

aj: Sounds like we need token-granular metrics rather than per-request. Field list I want emitted from runtime: kernel_name, batch_size, sequence_len, token_index, kv_hit (0/1), kv_latency_ms, compute_ms, mem_copy_ms, queue_ms, route, model_version, trace_id, token_size_bytes. Also export token_count and token_compute_ms (sum+count) for Prometheus-friendly aggregation.

mike: Agree. Dashboards I'd like: token latency waterfall (queue | kv | compute | postprocess), per-route cost-per-1k-tokens, kernel-version delta heatmap by seq_len, and a runtime-vs-billing diff panel. Also an alert when runtime-billing delta > 5% sustained for 30m.

sara: Prototype PromQL I used to get per-token compute ms by kernel: 

```
(sum by(route,kernel_name) (rate(token_compute_ms_sum[5m]))) / (sum by(route,kernel_name) (rate(token_compute_ms_count[5m])))
```

But note our current metric is exported as request-level sum/count, so the denominator is off for batched requests unless we emit per-token counts.

aj: Also we need a billing-aligned counter: billing_aligned_token_units. This should mirror invoiced units (including rounding rules, embeddings vs text mapping). If we emit that at ingestion we can show 'billing view' alongside 'runtime view' to find reconciliation gaps.

deploy-bot: deploy v2-kernel-selector started by aj at 2026-02-18T15:02Z :rocket:

liam: Do we have KV cache per-token granularity? Right now kv_hit is per-request which hides prefix reuse. We should instrument lookup_count and cache_hits at the KV layer (per-token) and expose kv_hit_rate_token = cache_hits / lookup_count.

sara: Regression timeline looks synchronous with the selector fallback logic — when the selector falls back to the non-quantized kernel for short seqs it increases compute_ms and also seems to touch KV less efficiently. I reproduced with a stress script. Snippet: 

```
$ ./stress_tokens.sh --route=translate --seq=64 --rps=200 --duration=2m
[run] kernel=v2 fallback=true avg_token_ms=6.2 compute_ms=4.9 kv_hit_rate=0.72
[run] kernel=v1 fallback=false avg_token_ms=5.0 compute_ms=3.8 kv_hit_rate=0.80
```

aj: Proposed action items: 1) add per-token KV metrics (lookup_count, cache_hits, kv_latency_ms) 2) implement billing_aligned_token_units counter and emit mapping logic in telemetry 3) add the dashboard panels Mike listed and a Grafana alert rule for runtime/billing delta >5% over 30m 4) add unit/integration test to kernel selector to prefer quantized-friendly kernels for seq_len < 128.

mike: I'll own dashboards/alerts. Can you give me example panel specs? For the waterfall panel I want stacked series: queue_ms, kv_latency_ms, compute_ms, postprocess_ms (all per-token averages). For the delta panel show: 100*(runtime_cost_per_token - billing_cost_per_token)/billing_cost_per_token.

sara: I'll open a small PR to runtime to emit token-level traces and KV per-token counters today (expect PR by EOD). I'll include a migration doc for the metrics team describing name changes and how billing_aligned_token_units should be derived. Also pinging finance later for rounding rules.

liam: One more: instrument kernel_selection_reason tag (e.g., "optimal", "fallback", "force_pin") so we can slice regressions by selection cause.

aj: Good call. Without that we can't correlate selector decisions to cost deltas.

mike: Once Sara's PR lands I can prototype panels. Also suggest a short-run synthetic test in prod-like to measure billing delta before and after selector changes.

sara: Will do. I'll also attach a tiny csv of the stress run results in the PR for quick validation in dashboards.

liam: Thanks all — let's track action items in the ticket I'll create and link the dashboard. :thumbsup:
